newsitem.title: UK: Britain's CBI supports unitary company boards.
newsitem.headline: Britain's CBI supports unitary company boards.

text.p: Britain's Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said on Thursday that unitary boards provide the best structure to pursue shareholder value and successful company performance.

In a report, the CBI said directors' main duty should be to shareholders and came out against customer, employee or supplier representatives, even though it recognised the interests of these groups must be taken into account.

Unitary boards, the norm in Britain, comprise a single board combining executive and non-executive directors. Two-tier boards, more common in the Netherlands and Germany, have a supervisory board of non-executives and a management board comprising company executives.
It said such members could have a conflict of interest between their duty to the company and to their constituency.
The CBI report was compiled as a contribution to a committee chaired by ICI Plc chairman Sir Ronald Hampel, which is looking into aspects of corporate governance.
The CBI report also urges the Hampel committee to look in detail at the case for and against distinguishing the liabilities of non-executive directors and executive directors.
